producedBy: read-only deployment telemetry and SRE investigation
sanitization: Aggregate counts, bounded timing summaries, and build identities only; raw logs, request bodies, SQL, host/process identifiers, and personal data omitted.

providerMetricsCoverage.averageCpuMemory: low per aggregate provider metrics; exact values not retained
providerMetricsCoverage.limitations: Only two readiness requests were returned; these aggregates do not establish user-request impact, active instance count, or absence of unobserved load.

providerMetrics.limitations: Only three requests were returned and all observed endpoint samples were readiness probes; zero 5xx points do not prove zero user-facing failures. The instance-count series is inconsistent.

reportedIdleWindows.ownerObservation: The owner reports no noticed downtime during active use; noticed interruptions occur while the app is idle or unused.
reportedIdleWindows.correlationMethod: Read-only log and metric samples around ±5 minutes of each reported time; this is temporal correlation, not request-level tracing.

providerCoverage.limitations: Endpoint metrics contained readiness probes only, not ordinary-user traffic. Zero observed 5xx points do not establish that user requests succeeded.

reportedIdleWindows.historicalSearchDiscrepancy: An Oct 21 exact-window search returned no records; the Nov 2 unrevision-filtered ±5-minute query found samples around these anchors. The reader/window discrepancy remains unresolved.

serverJobFailureReview.queryScope: Read-only production replica; live scope; failed scheduled-evaluation jobs completed in the interval. Selected only static job type, status, error codes, attempt counts/outcomes, and timestamps; actor IDs, input payloads, result data, and raw error messages were not returned.

boundedErrorMessageClassification.method: A SQL CASE expression inspected error-message text but returned only coarse category labels; raw messages were not selected or returned.
boundedErrorMessageClassification.limitation: Text-token classification is heuristic. Generic handler_failed codes and unclassified messages do not rule out database, provider, or application causes.

sourceReview.executionPath: The handler iterates dates for a scope and wraps each date's runWebPushAlerts call in the protected commit boundary. That path performs database work and serial external push sends before the boundary returns.
sourceReview.risk: A protected per-date operation can keep its job-row transaction/lock open while database calls and external push delivery run. This is a plausible pool/worker-pressure contributor, not a proven cause of the observed degradation.
sourceReview.errorBoundary: Provider send exceptions are caught and recorded by delivery handling; generic handler_failed receipts do not identify whether an uncaught database, cancellation, or other application error triggered the retry.
sourceReview.nextValidation: Use a synthetic slow-send test with pool acquisition and lease timing to measure the protected boundary. Do not change the production job boundary solely from temporal correlation.

serverJobFailureReview.reconciliation: The narrower 04:17–04:21Z query found two distinct failed jobs with six attempt receipts. A query matching the readiness sample's five-minute window found three failed and one cancelled job on the production read replica, versus five terminal failures reported by readiness. The time/window or telemetry-versus-replica discrepancy remains unresolved.

counterScope.poolCounters: Process-local pool measurements, not an Autoscale fleet aggregate.
counterScope.instanceMapping: No retained instance identity is available to map the process to one Autoscale instance.

assessment.finding: Production telemetry around the owner-reported idle windows and two Nov 2 periods shows recurring process-local pool contention overlapping with background-job, queue-monitor, rollover, outbox, and push-enqueue failures.
assessment.confidence: High that pool contention and worker failures recurred; moderate that they align with low-traffic/idle periods; low that they caused the reported interruptions or identify the initiating cause.
assessment.causeBoundary: Aggregated telemetry does not identify whether slow database work, event-loop stalls, or another upstream condition initiated the pressure, and cannot correlate an individual failed user request. Readiness success after an incident does not prove uninterrupted service.

nextDiagnostic.action: Correlate primary-database query and connection waits, per-instance pool/event-loop samples, request outcomes, and the five terminal scheduled-job failure details for 2026-11-02 04:17–04:21 UTC before changing configuration or infrastructure.

assessment.finding: Read-only telemetry shows recurring short-lived application-side, process-local database-pool contention on the serving build, with pool saturation, queued checkouts, acquisition errors, event-loop delay, and database-timeout warnings.
assessment.confidence: High that pool contention recurred; low that it caused user-visible downtime or identifies the initiating mechanism.
assessment.causeBoundary: Available aggregate telemetry cannot determine whether event-loop stalls, slow database work, or another upstream condition initiated the pressure, and cannot assign request-level causality.
assessment.impactBoundary: Provider metrics returned only a few readiness requests in the sampled windows and cannot establish ordinary-user impact or prove there were no failures.

latestLogSnapshot.captureMethod: Read-only deployment-log refresh; not a dedicated telemetry query
latestLogSnapshot.sanitization: Retained only aggregate counts, bounded timings, operation categories, and timestamps; omitted process/host identifiers, raw messages, payloads, and request records.
latestLogSnapshot.runCorrelation: No run-bound or request-level identity was present in this sampled evidence; this is not proof that the user-reported auto-tracking stop was caused by these stalls.
latestLogSnapshot.assessment: This later sample is consistent with repeated database-pool contention and includes long post-checkout work and event-loop delay. It makes backend contention a plausible contributor to delayed recovery, but does not identify the initiating cause or link the sample to a specific run. No production setting, data, or schema was changed.

wakeScreenshotWindow.captureMethod: Sanitized aggregates extracted from read-only deployment logs; screenshot time is approximate from owner-provided image.

ownerReportedBehavior.context: After switching from chat to the app
ownerReportedBehavior.limitations: No exact event time, active screen, request identity, or run-bound trace was supplied. This narrows the symptom but does not identify its cause.

additionalScreenshotPair.commonVisibleState: Still recovering: checking the current production state
additionalScreenshotPair.limitations: The status indicators differ across the screenshot pair while recovery remains visible. The matching production interval also shows severe pool and event-loop pressure, but there is no request/run correlation and no proof that this caused the UI or auto-tracking behavior.

wakeScreenshotWindow.limitations: The production pressure temporally overlaps the owner-reported wake/unresponsive screen, but aggregate telemetry does not identify the browser request or run and does not prove causation. Pool and event-loop measurements improved in the following sample. No production setting, data, or schema was changed.

aggregateEndpointMetrics.syncEvents: Long-duration requests observed; may be normal long-lived streams.
One long-duration request observed; may be a normal stream.
aggregateEndpointMetrics.autoTrackClaimRequestsInReturnedMetrics: None appeared in the endpoint list.

scheduledJobReviewWindow.result: Two failed jobs across six attempts; one lease_expired and remaining handler_failed.
scheduledJobReviewWindow.relevance: Not contemporaneous with the 19:01Z or 19:09Z wake windows; cannot explain those reports.

otherChecks.providerResourceSignal: CPU/memory aggregates and ordinary-route latency do not indicate host-wide saturation, but provider samples are sparse.

causalAssessment.finding: Recurring application-side database-pool contention and event-loop delay are the strongest measured contributor and overlap both wake reports. They could delay recovery and tracking, but do not prove why in-tab controls appeared inert or auto-tracking stopped.
causalAssessment.claimStormAssessment: The endpoint aggregates weakly argue against a simple repeated auto-track-claim storm; they cannot rule out a wake burst, identify the affected browser/run, or establish server-worker progress.
rankedAlternatives: Slow or timed-out canonical recovery leaves the client safety barrier active.
A client/browser resume or recovery-state defect remains plausible and unexcluded.
A host-wide CPU/memory saturation event is less supported by the sparse provider samples.
causalAssessment.limitations: No request/run correlation, exact worker events, or browser/OS lifecycle trace is available. Long sync/events durations may be normal open streams.

wakeRecoverySreInvestigation.nextDiagnostic: Capture one controlled, synchronized wake reproduction with privacy-safe client visibility, control-action, recovery, and auto-track outcomes. Pair each recovery with an ephemeral correlation token and server request status/duration plus per-instance pool, event-loop, and worker events. Do not retain payloads or personal identifiers.

laterDeploymentLogSnapshot.environment: Published production deployment logs, distinguished by SRE from the local API workflow.
laterDeploymentLogSnapshot.exactRevisionAttribution: The later snapshot does not embed a serving revision. The earlier SRE check identified revision 42763954-0c35-47c4-8b4b-6ea38c26deb1 as serving and found no newer build, but the later snapshot's revision is not independently confirmed.
laterDeploymentLogSnapshot.otherSignals: The queue monitor timed out, outbox reads were slow, and two production server-job runs failed with dependency-connection after about 13 seconds.
laterDeploymentLogSnapshot.assessment: This is a later recurrence of production pool pressure after the 19:01–19:10Z wake reports, not proof of continuous pressure between windows or of the cause of the phone's unresponsive controls or stopped tracking.

endpointMetricCheck.exactWindow: No endpoint rows were returned for /api/sync/today, /api/sync/events, or /api/sync/auto-track/claim; missing rows do not prove zero requests or success.
endpointMetricCheck.comparison: Earlier partial aggregates around the screenshots contained a small number of sync/today and sync/events requests; two auto-track claims had no 4xx/5xx in 18:59–19:04Z. Later missing endpoint rows do not establish absence of traffic.
endpointMetricCheck.limitation: No request, run, or device correlation is available, and the later pool-pressure evidence adds no direct sync-route status or latency.

screenshotObservation.interpretation: Owner reports the Pause tap appeared to work; this screenshot is not a server acknowledgement trace and does not identify which edits remain unconfirmed.

endpointMetrics.interpretation: One long-duration stream may be normal; it is not evidence by itself of a failed sync.

publishedLogSamples.eventLoopNumericDelay: unknown; two event-loop-related entries had no numeric delay

successfulWakeAttemptComparison.comparisonWithSeverePoolWindow: Sampled pool values are lower than the 19:29:56–19:32:00Z recurrence, which had 35 acquisition errors in each adjacent minute and up to 18 waiters. Sparse samples do not prove recovery or zero contention.
successfulWakeAttemptComparison.requestRunDeviceCorrelation: None available; aggregate metrics cannot identify the owner's device or run, and 4xx/5xx counts do not expose successful 2xx counts.

isolatedBrowserSyncPerformance.environment: Isolated Chromium browser; synthetic test, not production.
isolatedBrowserSyncPerformance.test: Measures canonical edit and foreground recovery latency
isolatedBrowserSyncPerformance.network: Loopback, 0/40ms injected request delay, no bandwidth cap
isolatedBrowserSyncPerformance.limitations: Loopback and injected-delay results do not represent production mobile networking, physical Android behavior, or OS-suspended JavaScript. Browser signal counts are retained without raw messages.

nextDiagnostic.action: Use a controlled wake reproduction with privacy-safe client state/action outcomes and an ephemeral correlation token, paired with server request outcomes, per-instance pool/event-loop data, and worker events. Separately reconcile the Oct 21 versus Nov 2 historical log-query discrepancy before changing infrastructure.
